title: Storage trait: FsStorage and MemoryStorage in both languages
description:
Replace the hard-wired filesystem access with a `Storage` trait (design §3.1).

## Steps
1. Specs first: `features/storage/memory_storage.feature` and `fs_storage.feature` (story "Storage is pluggable", plus list, stat, delete and search-index persistence through storage).
2. Rust `rust/src/storage.rs` with the trait from design §3.1: `list`, `read`, `write_atomic`, `delete`, `stat`, `lock` (a no-op guard is fine for now; V6a implements real locking) and `local_path`, plus the `Entry`, `Meta` and `LockGuard` types.
   - `FsStorage` (atomic temp file + rename, which is what exists today).
   - `MemoryStorage` (a `Mutex<BTreeMap<String, (Vec<u8>, Meta)>>`).
3. `Table` holds an `Arc<dyn Storage>`. Keep `Table::new(..., directory, ...)`, which means `FsStorage`, and add `Table::with_storage(...)`. `Database::from_schema_with_storage(...)`. The search index files (`.virtuus/index/...`) also go through storage.
4. Python: `python/src/virtuus/_python/storage.py` with the same two classes. `Table` and `Database` accept `storage=`.

## Acceptance
- `make check` green.
- `grep -nE "std::fs|fs::" rust/src/{table,database,search}.rs` shows nothing. All filesystem access lives in `storage.rs`.

## Verify
`make check PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python`, plus the grep above.
